time.desc: The leader of one country publicly stated that he would attack the other side's key civilian infrastructure and require the other side to give up access to the strait. Senior officials from the other side immediately warned that they might block another key waterway as a retaliatory option.
The party launching the air strikes announced a suspension of bombings and attacks on the other side for about two weeks, leaving a window for diplomatic negotiations.

After the ceasefire came into effect, third-party governments publicly stated that the ceasefire did not restrict their military operations in other battlefields, triggering disputes over the scope of the ceasefire and calls from other countries to expand its scope of application.

One party to the conflict announced that it would implement a naval blockade of the opponent's port and announced the start time. The relevant actions were advanced in parallel with the talks between the two parties.

The military of the party announcing the blockade officially launched the naval blockade of the opponent's port as planned and stated that it would not affect the freedom of navigation of ships in non-target ports.
The opponent's country held a large-scale memorial ceremony for the death of the late supreme leader, and the new supreme leader gave a tough speech, saying that his country shocked the world.
